purpose: Deterministic source mapping for direct quotations: each entry names the work, edition or translation, a locator, and where the exact wording can be checked. `match` is the wording as it appears in released pieces; the release-gate test fails if a mapped match is missing from a listed piece, if a quotation from a withheld ledger record appears in released data without an entry here, or if an untraced quotation reappears.

source.work: Legalize It All: How to win the war on drugs (Harper's Magazine, cover story / Report)
source.author: Dan Baum, quoting John Ehrlichman (Richard Nixon's domestic policy adviser) from a 1994 interview with Baum
source.edition_or_translation: Harper's Magazine, April 2016 issue (print and web). Opening paragraphs of the piece. Not Hari.
source.locator: Opening paragraphs, first page of the article. The interview was in 1994 (Baum gives no month or day). Print page numbers of the April 2016 issue not verified.
source.url: https://harpers.org/archive/2016/04/legalize-it-all/ (paywalled, HTTP 402 to my fetch); Wayback capture I read: https://web.archive.org/web/20161231234109/https://harpers.org/archive/2016/04/legalize-it-all/

quotations.note: Attributed to John Ehrlichman from a 1994 interview with Dan Baum, first published in Harper's in 2016. Not from Hari's 2015 book. Harper's prints 'black' and 'blacks' in lower case. A single-source account; Ehrlichman's family and several former Nixon aides dispute it. Released pieces say so.
